article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: EmergenC × Kush Mints
Breeder: Seed Junky Genetics / Cookies collab
THC Content: Commonly around 22–26%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , beta-caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Blood orange, tangerine, creamy citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to early October
Indoor Yield: 350–450 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 50–500 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Blood Moon is built around a flavor that cannabis rarely captures this clearly: dark, ripe orange with enough gas and earth underneath to keep it from tasting like ordinary citrus weed. The flower can carry flashes of amber, red, purple, and deep green beneath a dense resin coating, giving the cultivar an appropriately dramatic appearance.

Yet its effects are considerably more balanced than the name suggests. Rather than driving immediately toward sedation or stimulation, this hybrid often begins with an optimistic mental lift before introducing a comfortable full-body calm. That combination of blood-orange terpenes, Kush depth, and controlled potency has made the strain one of the more recognizable collaborations connected to Seed Junky Genetics and Cookies.
Genetics and Lineage

Blood Moon comes from EmergenC crossed with Kush Mints, bringing together a citrus-heavy modern hybrid and one of Seed Junky Genetics’ most influential mint-and-Kush cultivars. EmergenC carries Orange Push Pop and Sunset Sherbet genetics, which helps explain the unusually concentrated orange character inherited by the offspring. Kush Mints contributes a contrasting side built around earthy Kush, mint, gas, potency, and a more substantial physical presence. The result is not simply another orange strain; its citrus character is wrapped in creamy, earthy, and fuel-driven layers.

Both sides of the pedigree also influence the experience. EmergenC brings brightness and an energetic quality that keeps the opening from feeling excessively heavy, while Kush Mints adds enough physical calm to prevent the high from becoming overly sharp. Visually, well-grown plants can develop dense flowers with olive to darker green coloration, reddish-orange pistils, occasional purple shading, and abundant trichomes. The overall expression sits comfortably between its parents, combining modern dessert-style resin production with a much more distinctive citrus identity.
Effects and Experience

The first noticeable phase often arrives above the shoulders. Mood tends to brighten, conversation can become more engaging, and activities that felt routine a few minutes earlier may suddenly hold more interest. Creative thinking frequently accompanies the uplift, although the mental energy is generally smoother than that of a highly stimulating sativa. For experienced cannabis consumers, moderate amounts can work well for music , casual gaming , social gatherings, walking, or creative projects where relaxed attention is more useful than intense concentration.

A warmer body effect gradually develops beneath that mental lift. Muscular tension may soften and the pace of the experience becomes more comfortable without necessarily producing couch-lock. With larger doses, however, the balance moves toward heavier relaxation and hazier thinking. This makes the cultivar adaptable but also dose-sensitive. People accustomed to potent marijuana may find it unusually functional at modest amounts, whereas newer consumers can encounter dizziness, dry mouth, red eyes, or anxious thinking if they consume too much too quickly.
Medical Benefits

Medical cannabis consumers sometimes gravitate toward balanced hybrids when they want noticeable relaxation without abandoning daytime functionality. Blood Moon’s combination of elevated mood and physical ease may appeal to adults using marijuana to manage everyday stress, temporary low mood, appetite difficulties, or physical discomfort. The later body relaxation may also make the cultivar useful during the transition from daytime responsibilities into a quieter evening.

Strain names should never be treated as medical guarantees, however. Cannabis flower varies between harvests, and THC concentration, terpene levels, minor cannabinoids, and individual physiology all influence the response. A dose that feels calming to one person may feel overstimulating to another. Anyone using marijuana for persistent pain, anxiety, sleep problems, or another diagnosed condition should consider tested cannabinoid levels, possible medication interactions, and professional medical advice rather than relying exclusively on a cultivar’s reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Blood orange defines the aromatic center of this strain. Opening a container can release a concentrated combination of orange peel, ripe tangerine, sweet citrus oil, and darker fruit notes, followed almost immediately by a splash of gasoline. The Kush influence emerges after the brighter aromas settle, contributing damp earth, faint mint, pepper, and creamy sweetness. Some batches develop a slightly funky quality that makes the citrus smell deeper and less candy-like than varieties built purely around orange terpenes.

Limonene naturally complements the bright citrus character, while beta-caryophyllene adds peppery spice and myrcene contributes an earthy, herbal foundation. On the inhale, creamy orange and sweet tangerine often dominate. The exhale changes direction, bringing soil, Kush, spice, and lingering fuel across the palate. That progression is one of the cultivar’s strongest qualities: the flavor begins almost refreshing but finishes considerably heavier, preventing the orange profile from becoming thin or one-dimensional.
Growing Information

Blood Moon is best approached as an intermediate-level cannabis plant because reliable results depend more on canopy and environmental management than complicated feeding techniques. Indoors, topping during vegetative growth can encourage several productive branches instead of one dominant central stem. Low-stress training or a screen can then spread those branches across the available light. An indoor flowering period of roughly eight to ten weeks is a reasonable expectation, although phenotype and environmental conditions can shift the finishing date.

As flowers gain weight, consistent air circulation becomes increasingly important. Resinous, tightly formed buds can retain moisture inside their structure even when the surrounding room feels dry. Growers should therefore avoid allowing humidity to remain elevated late in bloom. Outdoors, sunny conditions and a reasonably dry early autumn offer the best opportunity for healthy maturation, with harvest commonly falling around late September into early October. Moderate indoor yields are realistic, while outdoor plants can become considerably more productive when given unrestricted root space, adequate nutrition, and full-season sunlight.
FAQ
Is Blood Moon indica or sativa?

Blood Moon is generally considered a balanced hybrid. Its character combines an uplifting, creative mental effect with gradually increasing body relaxation, rather than leaning heavily toward either classic sativa stimulation or indica sedation.
What are the genetics of Blood Moon?

The established Cookies and Seed Junky version comes from EmergenC crossed with Kush Mints. EmergenC contributes prominent orange and creamy fruit qualities, while Kush Mints supplies earthy Kush, mint, gas, potency, and physical relaxation.
How strong is Blood Moon?

Commercial flower commonly falls around the low-to-mid 20% THC range, although individual harvests can test higher or lower. Its balanced effects can make the potency feel deceptively manageable at first, so THC-sensitive consumers should still begin with a modest dose.
What does Blood Moon taste like?
Blood orange and tangerine lead the flavor, followed by creamy citrus, earth, pepper, sweet Kush, and gas. Some examples also produce light mint or herbal notes on the finish.
Is Blood Moon good for daytime use?

Moderate amounts can work well during the afternoon or early evening for experienced consumers because the initial effect often feels happy, clear-headed, and creative. Larger doses are more likely to produce heavier physical relaxation and reduced concentration.
Final Thoughts on Blood Moon

Blood Moon earns its place among modern citrus hybrids by doing more than simply smelling like oranges. EmergenC provides a vivid blood-orange foundation, while Kush Mints brings earth, cream, gas, and enough physical weight to transform that brightness into something considerably richer. The result has a recognizable aromatic signature rather than the interchangeable candy profile found in many contemporary crosses.

Its effects follow the same principle of contrast. The opening is cheerful and mentally engaging, yet relaxation steadily develops without necessarily ending in immediate sedation. Experienced cannabis consumers looking for flavorful weed that can bridge the gap between daytime uplift and evening calm should find plenty of versatility here. Combined with colorful, resin-heavy flower and a memorable citrus-gas finish, Blood Moon offers a well-rounded expression of two prominent modern genetic lines.
